To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the determinants of public–private health care expenditure split include per capita income, income distribution variables, and federal government health transfers.
the public–private health care split has been driven primarily by long term economic factors and by the federal government’s decision to reduce health transfers.

the public share of total health expenditures is negatively associated with the share of income held by the highest income quintile, positively associated with the share held by the lowest income quintile, and negatively associated with per capita income.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of the public– private mix of health care financing in Canada over the period 1985–1996.
the public/private split in Canadian health care spending.
the issue of how the public–private balance in health care spending is affected by economic and policy forces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public–private share is a function of the long term forces of economic development and of the short term policy choices of governments.
the increase in the share of private health care expenditures is partly due to the policy choice of reducing federal transfers to the provinces.
the public-private split in Canadian health care expenditure is determined by both long term economic and short term political factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increase in the share of private expenditures is the result of both economic and policy factors.
the private share of Canadian health care expenditures is determined primarily by economic factors.

, as the public–private health expenditure mix is a function of both economic and policy variables, it is not surprising that the public–private share of health spending in Canada is not converging to that of other OECD countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public–private health spending mix is determined by a combination of long term economic forces, the structure of government transfers and policy choices.
the public-private split in health care spending is not simply a matter of economic forces, but also reflects the policy choices made by governments.
the public–private balance in health care spending in Canada is largely a reflection of the underlying economic forces that shape the demand and supply of health care.
